## The same customers, three answers

App installers spend more, but they also differ before installing. The three blue bars compare the naive difference, a linear adjustment, and **double machine learning (DML)** from the lab. The orange bars show the extra spend needed to pay for your install credit at 30% margin. Move the omitted-confounder slider to see how fragile the DML decision is to a common cause missing from the data. The slider applies a sensitivity shift; it does not refit the model.

**Work one example.** A $2.50 credit requires $8.33 of extra spend at 30% margin. DML estimates $13.51, with a 95% interval of $10.51–$16.50. The lower end clears break-even. A $6.39 omitted-variable shift, as measured when the module leaves out mobile share, moves the whole interval below or across break-even and changes the recommendation.

**Data.** [Seeded synthetic app-install customers](https://github.com/project-delphi/ml-for-growth-marketing/blob/main/data/synthetic/app_install_customers.csv), with known treatment effects. Estimates and the leave-one-variable-out shift come from the [module's recorded run](../modules/15-double-ml.qmd). A real credit campaign would need randomization to measure how many installs the credit persuades.
